response: I have not used any generative AI tools outside of coursework
Editing, rephrasing, and simplifying existing work with feedback (e.g., revising drafts, debugging code, checking calculations, making complex material more understandable)

Over 2 years ago I used ChatGPT to help summarize lengthy material. Then I did not use any AI for 2 years as I do not support the increase of AI tools in most all regards- due to the direct consequences our planet faces as well as the studies already showing a connection to decreased cognitive abilities for everyday AI users. 
Anyway- this semester I use ChatGPT only when I am stuck on a Python code and Google does not help. It has only been a handful of times and I feel horrible each time.
I have not used AI outside of my coursework
Always available when I needed help; Easy access to information and resources; Enhanced understanding through clear, tailored explanations

Spent excessive time trying to get AI to work properly; Received poor quality, unreliable, or biased information from AI; Received contradictory responses from AI within the same conversation; Experienced reduced skills, understanding, or over-dependence on AI; Had AI make me second-guess my own knowledge or abilities; Felt that my work lost its personal voice or creativity; Felt pressured to use AI because others were using it; Witnessed unfair advantages when some students used AI and others did not

For hundreds of years humans have learned in their own time, fashion, etc. I think it is a disgrace that AI is even in the conversation of education, as it actively diminishes learning capabilities and critical thinking skills under the guise of a 'tool'. Its a tool for cheating, period.
